highlights: Camera calibration no longer labels the target's rings wrongly when some look solid in a small, dim or noisy photo; it says what to fix instead, and no longer reports a mirrored picture by mistake.
Calibration keeps only the lens terms the photo supports, so the camera picture stays closer to the burn at the bed's corners, outside the target's rings.
A camera looking straight down without a measured height is graded as lined up at the target sheet's height only, and asks for the camera height so other thicknesses line up.
The camera overlay no longer shows a folded copy of the picture where the camera cannot see. Camera setup adds Ring size for low-resolution cameras and names the size to use when rings are too small.
Camera setup can put the ring target on the canvas to engrave like any job, asks to home the machine first, and says when a calibration was made before the bed position was known.
Job Review warns when artwork is placed with the camera but Start from is not Absolute Coordinates, because the job would burn somewhere else.
